title: Hierarchical role templates and SCIM change-stream for quarterly access recertification
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Context: Our compliance program requires quarterly access recertification across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private tenants. Current manual reviews are noisy and inconsistent: RBAC roles are duplicated across orgs, SCIM syncs can drop deltas, and SSO session policies are heterogeneous per customer. This ticket standardizes cross-tenant role templates (hierarchical, auditable), emits a SCIM change-stream for delta detection, and wires both into an automated quarterly recertification workflow with one-click remediation and audit evidence exports.

Goals:
- Provide hierarchical role templates (org -> team -> scoped roles) that map to existing RBAC primitives and support inheritance and exceptions.
- Implement a SCIM change-stream (evented) that reliably emits add/modify/remove events for accounts and group memberships with sequence numbers for idempotency.
- Add enforcement for SAML session expiry and session-to-role mapping in the auth pipeline.
- Build a quarterly recertification workflow: digest generation, reviewer UI links, auto-remediation suggestions, and signed evidence export for auditors.

Scope (MVP):
- Role template schema and API to create/update templates.
- SCIM change-stream producer (Kafka topic + compacted consumer) and a lightweight consumer service that powers recertification lists.
- Integration with existing Console: reviewer UI route that lists out-of-sync accounts with one-click revoke/grant buttons and records decisions in audit log.
- Evidence export: PDF + CSV export per tenant with signed hash and timeline.

Out of scope (for follow-ups):
- Cross-org delegated approval flows (future project).
- Rich policy language (we'll start with allow/deny/inherit).

Acceptance criteria:
1) Role templates API is implemented, schema documented, and E2E tests cover inheritance and exception cases.
2) SCIM change-stream emits consistent sequence numbers; consumer can rehydrate state from an offset.
3) Console reviewer view lists pending recertifications for a tenant and allows approve/revoke; actions create audit events visible in Logs.
4) Evidence export contains all decisions and a signed manifest; exports stored in tenant-residency buckets per data residency setting.
5) Automated smoke tests validate recertification run weekly in staging and send alerts on failures.

Implementation approach:
- Schema: define hierarchical role template JSON with an explicit inheritance path. Store templates in the config service with versioning.
- SCIM: extend scim-syncer to produce change events to the new scim-changes Kafka topic. Use compacted topics + sequence numbers to support replays.
- Consumer: small Go service (recertification-runner) that consolidates SCIM deltas and current RBAC state and emits reviewer lists into the Console service via an internal API.
- Console: add reviewer route and action endpoints; actions call internal auth service to make changes and write audit events.
- Evidence: export generator runs after recertification and signs manifest with KMS.

Rollout and migration plan:
1) Feature flag SCIM change-stream per region.
2) Deploy role templates API in shadow mode (no enforcement) and run a sync job to map existing roles.
3) Enable reviewer UI in beta for selected tenants; gather feedback.
4) Gradually enable enforcement after 2 successful recertification cycles and qa sign-off.

Testing and QA:
- Unit tests for schema validation and inheritance logic.
- Integration tests: scim-syncer -> kafka -> recertification-runner -> console action path.
- Load test: simulate 10k accounts and group churn to ensure consumer keeps up and Kafka retention/compact settings are adequate.
- Security review: verify KMS signing, access controls, and SAML session enforcement; penetration test checklist.

Monitoring and SLOs:
- Consumer lag < 30s for typical churn; alert if > 2 minutes.
- Recertification-runner errors < 0.1% of processed events.
- Evidence export success rate 100% within 10 minutes of completion.

Risks and trade-offs:
- Strong schema and enforcement may break customers with ad-hoc roles; opting for shadow mode mitigates risk.
- Compacted Kafka topics reduce storage but require careful sequence handling.
- One-click remediation trades rapid cleanup for potential for escalations; require reviewer confirmation and soft-revert window.

Open decisions:
- Locking strategy for template updates during an active recertification run (proposal: optimistic version check + short-lived lock).
- Whether to centralize evidence storage or allow tenant-specific residency buckets (early preference: tenant-residency per compliance requirements).

Success metrics:
- Reduce manual time per recertification by 70% for admins.
- 100% of tenants have an evidence export available within 15 minutes after run completion.

Notes on related work: Relies on ENG-4217 for baseline access-control schema and ENG-7482 for compliance evidence pipeline. See linked design doc for sequence diagrams and example templates.
